meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'along; by; about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('extreme, end, last').

examples.text: Но, по крайней мере, он дочь свою любит!
examples.trans: But at least he loves his daughter!
Who is last in the queue?

examples.text: Витя, я выражаю тебе своё крайнее возмущение!
examples.trans: Vitya, I express to you my extreme outrage!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'measure, degree' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The preventive measure remains the same.

examples.text: Мера пресечения остаётся прежней. Домашний арест!
examples.trans: The preventive measure remains the same. House arrest!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'daddy; folder' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Or else his daddy helped him out.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая папочка.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new daddy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.
Are you doing anything about it?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'биться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to achieve, win over', paired with 'добиваться'.

examples.text: Я всё равно вас добьюсь, Марина!
examples.trans: I will win you over anyway, Marina!

examples.text: Мы оба сами многого добились в жизни.
examples.trans: We both achieved a lot in life on our own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'годить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait'.

examples.trans: Wait. Maybe everything will still work out.

examples.text: Погоди, нам нужна более объективная оценка.
examples.trans: Wait, we need a more objective opinion.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in front of, before', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

постоять.gloss: to stand for a while; to wait

meanings.en: to stand for a while; to wait
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stand for a while; to wait', paired with 'стоять'.

examples.trans: I'll stand here for a bit.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'after', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to prepare, to cook, to make
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ваня, всё гораздо хуже. Меня обманули.
examples.trans: Vanya, it's much worse than that. I've been cheated.
Vanya, it's much worse than that.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.
